explanation: As in much of the world, pointing directly at a person with the index finger can come across as rude or confrontational in Greece, with an open-hand gesture viewed as more polite. This is a general social-courtesy norm rather than a severe taboo, and pointing at objects or directions is far less sensitive than pointing at a person.
local_tip: When indicating a person or direction, gesture with an open hand rather than a single extended finger.
regional_note: In casual settings among friends or in cosmopolitan cities, this is treated more loosely than in formal or elder-respect contexts.

also_check.note: Index-finger pointing is seen as very rude; an open hand or gentle nod is preferred.
Pointing is taboo, especially with the left hand; an open palm or thumb is used instead.
Index-finger pointing is common and generally acceptable in casual contexts.
